newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police in money laundering breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: German police in money laundering breakthrough.

text.p: German police said on Tuesday they had detained five men in a major operation against money laundering in the drugs trade.

German police said a Dutchman suspected of converting around 120 million marks ($79.81 million) into foreign currency in Germany had been detained as he tried to change several hundred pounds sterling at a bank in the Belgian city of Antwerp.

"The money seized was not counterfeit, but most probably dirty drug money which was to be laundered," police said in a statement, adding he had the ideal pretext to change large amounts of money as he owned two Dutch bureaux de change.
German, Dutch and Belgian police cooperated in the operation.
Police said the man was caught on October 10 and four more people were detained in the Netherlands a few days later.
One of those arrested was a German who owned a book store and a coffee shop in Amsterdam. Police recovered 50 kg (110 lbs) of hashish in a search of the bookstore.
The operation to track and detain the suspects lasted 2-1/2 years, German police said.
There were no further details. ($1=1.5034 Mark)
